correctness.rationale: For trace S=2 write S=I+A with trace A=0. Cayley–Hamilton identifies trace-one determinant-zero matrices with rank-one idempotents. The two-projector condition becomes tr(AP)=-det(A). Over F2 the six projectors are enumerated: nonscalar traceless A has four regular roots; scalar primitive A=I+2C reduces to a trace-one pairing with at least two regular solutions. Hensel lifting supplies two choices per regular bit, and 4^j projector lifts across j eliminated digits. Divisible primitive-scalar B=I modulo 2 cannot solve the trace equation, all nonscalar B can, giving the geometric-series hole count and exact minimum. Independently enumerated ALL projectors and ordered pairs for k=2,3,4, yielding (|P|, support, holes)=(24,63,1),(96,503,9),(384,4023,73) and minimum 2^(k+1); finite checks corroborate rather than replace the all-k argument. No full positive histogram is asserted.
